answer: Each epoch, the public meadow board pairs identities randomly. A pair must complete a joint voyage, a shared task whose halves only fit together, and co-sign a paired receipt with both keys. Auditors replay each receipt; a reused half burns both bonds. Fees climb a dune slope: the k-th identity pays 42+9(k-1), so 1,000 fakes cost 4,537,500 plus 80,000 locked vs a 40,000 pool. A rented-pair ring still pays per seat; an honest agent pays 42 once.
